findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P1] pilotFreezeCheck freezes N at the Wilson LOWER bound, which is NOT conservative under the pooled two-proportion formula: n peaks where pbar=(p1+(p1-mde))/2 is nearest 0.5, so a lower bound below ~0.5+mde/2 yields a SMALLER n than the observed baseline (counterexample: pilot 36/60, CI width 0.2406 freezes, lower 0.47366 -> 56/arm vs observed 0.60 -> 62/arm). The plan S7 wording (freeze at lower bound, conservative) shares the flaw. Fix the tool: freeze at the N-MAXIMIZING baseline within the Wilson CI (analytic max at p*=0.5+mde/2 clamped to the CI), document the deviation from the S7 letter as satisfying its conservative INTENT; flag plan S7 for a docs follow-up.
findings.resolvedReason: pilotFreezeCheck freezes at the N-maximizing baseline within the Wilson 95% CI (p*=0.5+mde/2 clamped); interpretation recorded in output; selfcheck pins the counterexample 36/60 -> frozen 62/arm vs buggy lower-bound 56, and the tight-CI case 42/60 -> 0.625 -> 62. Commit c562db46e. Plan S7 wording flagged for a docs follow-up (chip task_36a80fa5).

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P1] buildLedger binds only the protocolHash, not the frozen task-class MEMBERSHIP: validateManifest accepts trapClass not-in-protocol with trapGroup in_store, so unregistered fixtures can enter the run under a valid protocol hash. Fix: consume doc.taskClasses from guardFrozenProtocol and reject rows whose trapClass is not a member of the frozen group matching its trapGroup; add selfcheck case.
findings.resolvedReason: validateMembership added and called from build AND verify: every manifest row trapClass must be a member of the frozen protocol group matching its trapGroup; selfcheck cases: unregistered class refused, clean class declared in_store refused. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P2] The adequacy report includes only unpaired reference sizing; M5 requires unpaired reference + McNemar paired sizing. Fix: add a paired section (McNemar nPairs at the live point and the seeded band max, discordant cells derived under the documented independence approximation p01=p1(1-p2), p10=p2(1-p1), with optional explicit override in config) to adequacy-report.json and .md; add selfcheck case.
findings.resolvedReason: Adequacy report now includes McNemar paired sizing per population (derivePairedDiscordance independence approximation, protocol perPopulation.paired override supported): live 296 pairs, seeded band-max 65 pairs; md + json + selfcheck. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P2] Protocol validation rejects only inStore/heldOut overlap; a class can be in clean AND a fault group although clean tasks must never pool into the fault baseline. Fix: reject pairwise overlap across all three groups; add selfcheck case.
findings.resolvedReason: All-pairs overlap rejection across inStore/heldOut/clean with the offending classes named; selfcheck case clean/in-store overlap. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P2] Seals are self-authenticating (tamper+rehash passes) and validateFrozenProtocol ignores the sidecar protocolHash field it stores. Partial fix in-scope: verify sidecar.protocolHash === doc.protocolHash; document the threat model (tamper-EVIDENCE for accidental drift; external anchoring of the protocolHash into story/run evidence is the M6 runner responsibility). Full external anchoring is out of S1 scope by design.
findings.resolvedReason: Sidecar protocolHash now verified against protocol.json (selfcheck case added); threat model documented in code: seals are tamper-evidence for accidental drift, external anchoring of protocolHash into run/story evidence is the M6/M7 runner responsibility. Full external anchoring deliberately out of S1 scope. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P3] guardImmutable has a TOCTOU window between the guard and the three renames. Fix: re-check the guard immediately before the writes (narrows the window; single-host tooling tier documented).
findings.resolvedReason: guardImmutable re-checked immediately before the three ledger writes, narrowing the TOCTOU window; single-host tooling tier documented in the comment. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P3] protocol-selfcheck leaks the two extra mkdtemp roots (ablation-p1/p2) and snapDir (never removed in finally). Fix: track and remove all temp roots.
findings.resolvedReason: protocol-selfcheck tracks all extra mkdtemp roots (p1/p2/snapDir) and removes them in finally. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex P3] protocol.mjs usage line is inaccurate per subcommand (hash needs only --config; validate needs no --config; freeze takes experimentId from the config). Fix: per-subcommand usage output.
findings.resolvedReason: Per-subcommand usage lines: freeze (experimentId from config), validate (no config), hash (config only). Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: sample-size.mjs main() has no try/catch wrapper: JSON.parse failures (malformed config file) and readFileSync errors (file not found) surface as raw Node.js stack traces rather than the clean 'ERROR: <message>' pattern used consistently by protocol.mjs and pair-ledger.mjs. The quality review scope explicitly requires 'JSON parse failures produce useful errors'. Demonstration: node sample-size.mjs report --config=/nonexistent.json exits 1 but emits a 10-line stack trace from node:fs:442 instead of a clean ERROR line. Fix: wrap main() body in try { ... } catch (err) { console.error('ERROR: ' + err.message); process.exit(1); }
findings.resolvedReason: sample-size main() wrapped in try/catch emitting ERROR:<message> with exit 1, matching the other two CLIs. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: sample-size.mjs uses plain writeFileSync (not atomic temp-then-rename) for both adequacy-report.json and adequacy-report.md writes (lines 262-263). protocol.mjs and pair-ledger.mjs both define and use a writeAtomic(path, text) helper that writes to a .tmp-<pid> path then renames. A crash or SIGKILL between the two writeFileSync calls leaves a valid .json alongside a truncated or absent .md, and a crash mid-write leaves a half-written .json. The quality review scope requires atomic writes for every artifact write. Fix: add writeAtomic helper matching protocol.mjs pattern and use it for both output files.
findings.resolvedReason: adequacy-report.json/.md now written via writeAtomic (temp-then-rename), same helper pattern as the other tools. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: protocol-selfcheck.mjs leaks three temporary directories that are not cleaned up in the finally block: (1) the h1 root created at line 68 via mkdtempSync for the 'same config at different createdAt -> same protocolHash' test; (2) the h2 root created at line 69 for the same test; (3) snapDir created at line 107 for the directory-snapshot hashing test. Only the main 'tmp' root is cleaned via rmSync in the finally block (line 121). pair-ledger-selfcheck.mjs correctly wraps all secondary roots in their own try/finally blocks. Impact is minor (OS temp cleanup on reboot), but inconsistent with the hermetic selfcheck requirement.
findings.resolvedReason: Same fix as F-007 (duplicate finding from the quality lane): all extra mkdtemp roots removed in finally. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: CHK-003:edge:1 verificationIntent states 'increasing pd while holding the ratio (p01/p10) fixed does not increase the required pair count' (a claim about the ratio-fixed direction, where N decreases: verified - 77 pairs at ratio 3:1, pd=0.40 drops to 50 pairs at ratio 3:1, pd=0.60). However the selfcheck test labeled 'same asymmetry with more total discordance -> more pairs' exercises a DIFFERENT invariant: d fixed at 0.20, pd increases from 0.40 to 0.60 -> 77 to 116 pairs (more pairs, a correct but opposite-direction fact). The McNemar code is mathematically correct; this is a test-specification alignment gap where the selfcheck covers a valid-but-different monotonicity case than the one cited in the checklist.
findings.resolvedReason: Ratio-fixed monotonicity case added (pd 0.20 vs 0.40 at 3:1 ratio -> 155 vs 77 pairs, decreasing), alongside the existing fixed-d and fixed-pd invariants. Commit c562db46e.

findings.desc: [host-2 Codex re-verdict] Regression introduced by c562db46e: renderAdequacyMarkdown closing paragraph still described the M6 pilot rule as freeze at the Wilson 95% CI lower bound, contradicting the corrected F-001 implementation (N-maximizing baseline within the CI). Generated reports would carry the disproven rule text.
findings.resolvedReason: renderAdequacyMarkdown closing paragraph rewritten to state the corrected rule (freeze at the N-maximizing baseline within the Wilson 95% CI; lower bound alone not conservative, ref F-001). Selfcheck still green (29/29). Commit follows c562db46e.

The function body at lines 130-133 and 151 already carry the corrected narrative; only the top-level bullet in the file docstring was not updated.
